title: Preclinical Imaging XNAT-enabled Informatics (PIXI) Center
text:
Preclinical imaging is a critical component in the evaluation of drugs and development of imaging strategies to
diagnosis disease and assess/predict response to therapy. We enhance the development of a preclinical
imaging informatics platform and establish a data management and sharing (DMS) center to enhance
reproducibility, open science, and enable discovery in support of NCI’s precision medicine initiative.

title: Defining the role of single-cell heterogeneity in bacterial vaginosis
text:
Despite extensive characterization, we struggle to understand and control the progression of human-associated
microbial communities, including bacterial vaginosis (BV), a condition that is directly impactful to women’s health
and the acquisition of sexually transmitted infections. This proposal investigates single-cell genomic and
transcriptomic heterogeneity as two underexplored areas that impact the progression of BV. This intellectually
and methodologically innovative research will transform our understanding of the development, treatment, and
recurrence of BV and will provide broad-reaching insights into new strategies to prevent and treat polymicrobial
infections.

title: Temporal control of mitochondrial mutagenesis
text:
As we age, mutations accumulate inside our cells that limit energy production, contributing to various forms of
age-related pathology, including muscle wasting and neurodegeneration. In this application, we propose to
determine when these mutations arise, what happens to them as we grow older and whether they can be
selectively removed from our cells. Together, these experiments will help us gain a deeper understanding of
the aging process itself, guide the development of treatments that are aimed at treating age-related disease,
and help us determine when these treatments should be administered.

title: Yale Diagnostic Center of Excellence for Undiagnosed Diseases
text: The Undiagnosed Disease Network (UDN) is committed to ending the diagnostic odyssey for patients and families affected by undiagnosed disease. The proposed YDCoE brings together extensive clinical expertise, novel machine-learning clinical review tools, undiagnosed and rare disease discovery, next-gen sequencing and new approaches in bioinformatics and functional genomics to deliver clinical capacity for the UDN at unprecedented scale. Our strong community partnerships will ensure expanded access to individuals and groups who historically have not benefited from modern diagnostic investigations due to race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status or other systemic barriers.

title: Dissecting the Role Ubiquitin E3 Ligase UBR5 in Lymphomagenesis
text:
The ubiquitin E3 ligase, UBR5 has been found mutated in a significant number of patients (~18%) with mantle
cell lymphoma (MCL) with the majority of mutations identified in UBR5 were frame shift mutations found within
the HECT domain. Here we will study the molecular function of ubiquitin E3 ligase, UBR5 mutations in
lymphomagenesis. Deciphering the role of the UBR5 in mantle cell lymphoma will provide clues to lymphoma
transformation with the goal of identifying targets for future therapeutics.

title: UFM1 as a Modifier of Tau Pathology in Alzheimer Disease and Related Tauopathies
text:
The UFM1 cascade has very recently been identified as a major modifier of tau aggregation and changes in the
amount of conjugated UFM1 have been associated with pathological tau in human Alzheimer disease brain. The
project will use brain samples with different tauopathies and tau pathologies to determine changes in UFM1 and
their associations with tau in human disease, identify the substrates of UFM1 in brain and test mechanistically
whether and how the UFM1 cascade modifies tau levels and aggregation in vitro and in vivo. This will clarify if
the UFM1 pathway can be used as a possible therapeutic avenue for tauopathies.

title: BIOSPECIMEN REPOSITORY STORAGE SERVICES
text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a syndrome commonly defined by a single physiological feature–chronic airflow obstruction. To improve diagnosis and treatment of COPD, it is essential to divide this complex syndrome into biologically meaningful subgroups of COPD patients and to predict disease progression accurately within those subtypes. Our primary approaches to assess COPD progression will use physiology (i.e., FEV1 decline) and imaging (i.e., increased emphysema); however, we will also assess clinical characteristics (e.g., increased exacerbations) and epidemiology (e.g., increased mortality). We will apply imaging, physiology, epidemiology, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, epigenetics, and genetics to a 15-year longitudinal cohort of smokers to provide new insights into COPD progression. Longitudinal analysis of physiological and imaging data will provide valuable information regarding progression (or stability) of airflow obstruction, CT measurements of emphysema and airway disease, and clinical characteristics. Longitudinal analysis of Omics data will identify biomarkers of COPD progression within disease subtypes. Machine learning and network analysis of multiple Omics data will implicate pathobiological mechanisms for COPD progression. Genetic association analysis using existing whole genome sequencing (WGS) data will identify both rare and common genetic determinants of COPD progression. Integrating WGS with RNA-Seq, DNA methylation, metabolomics, and proteomics will also facilitate identification of functional variants within regions of genetic association.

title: Protein phosphatase 2A mediates influenza-induced inhibition of lung alveolar defense
text:
Influenza virus is a major cause of severe lung infection that is often complicated by secondary bacterial
coinfection. Viral-bacterial coinfections cause lung injury with high mortality and substantially contribute to
healthcare and disease burden. This research proposal aims to achieve new understanding of how influenza
virus promotes coinfection with Staphylococcus aureus (SA) to cause severe lung disease, with the overall goal
of developing novel therapeutic approaches for influenza-SA coinfection.

title: Discovering Drug-Like Probes for the α9α10 Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor
text:
The nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) are ligand-gated ion channels whose various subtypes have
been targeted in many central nervous system diseases and disorders. The α9α10 nAChR has been implicated
as a drug target for neuropathic pain, but very few drug-like and selective ligands have been developed. This
research project will fill this gap by developing an α9α10 nAChR-selective antagonist with promising drug-like
properties to further study this receptor’s role in neuropathic pain.

title: Genetic determinants of Bacteroides vulgatus colonization fitness and host inflammatory responses
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because the discovery of mechanisms by
prevalent bacterial members of the human gut microbiome colonize the gut and regulate
intestinal inflammation is expected to lead to new approaches for modifying microbiome
composition and new treatments for the human inflammatory bowel diseases and other
inflammatory disorders. The proposed research is therefore relevant to the part of NIH’s mission
that pertains to developing fundamental new knowledge that will enhance health and reduce the
burdens of illness.

title: Increasing the Yield and Utility of Pediatric Genomic Medicine with Exomiser
text:
Rare genetic diseases are collectively a common cause of morbidity in children and, despite advances in
genomic sequencing, precision clinical management is often hindered by the difficulties in making an accurate
and precise diagnosis. Here, we will extend our widely used diagnostic tool Exomiser to meet current
challenges and opportunities in pediatrics by improving its utility in clinical diagnostic contexts, adding
algorithms for new long-read sequencing technologies, expanding our reach to non-Mendelian rare diseases,
incorporating large-language models and other sophisticated machine learning algorithms, and providing new
approaches to analyze groups of unsolved cases to identify novel disease etiologies.

title: Dissecting stress granule dependencies in leukemia stem cells
text:
In this project, we utilize cutting edge proteomics and custom-designed functional screens to identify novel
RNA binding proteins important for hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) fate, and characterize their targets by
enhanced CLIP-seq and other genomics methods. If successful, these insights will provide fundamental
insights into regulation of hematopoiesis, supporting translational research in leukemia and other diseases of
the hematopoietic system.

title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Predict Cognitive Training Response in Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment
text:
Project Narrative/Relevance to Public Health:
Patients in the early stages of Alzheimer’s disease each display a unique pattern of altered brain structure, function,
and thinking and memory skills. Knowing that their diagnosis of amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) places
them at risk for developing Alzheimer’s disease, patients often seek out intervention to delay the progression of the
disease without knowing whether it will truly provide benefit. This project will use advanced machine learning tools to
provide detailed predictions of aMCI patients’ likelihood of improving from a widely supported cognitive training
intervention, and clarify how an individual patient’s brain and cognitive features contribute to their response-to-
intervention.

title: Single-cell based diagnostic platform with single-molecular transcriptional response profiling for rapid phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing of gonorrhea
text:
The main goal of this project is to develop and validate a rapid diagnostic platform capable of performing
antimicrobial susceptibility testing of Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG) using molecular RNA levels on a
programmable microfluidic single-cell analysis platform.

title: The SDOH-Homecare Intervention Focus Team (SHIFT) Trial to Mitigate SDOH in Stroke Outcomes and Build Community Capacity
text: Stroke is the leading cause of adult disability in the US with the greatest human and economic cost among individuals with a high burden of adverse social determinants of health (SDOH). It is increasingly clear that SDOH such as health care access and quality, availability of support services, educational opportunity and attainment, income, housing, transportation, health literacy etc., are major drivers of stroke outcomes. Demonstrating improved individual level stroke outcomes as a result of our SDOH Homecare Intervention Focus Team (SHIFT) and showing the impact of SHIFT on the health care system level may result in a paradigm shift in the approach to treating stroke patients with high SDOH burden and close the gap in health care disparities in this and other medical conditions.

title: Transcriptional Mutagenesis and Oxidative DNA Repair: Novel Mechanism and Therapeutic Target in Heart Failure
text:
Heart failure (HF) is often driven by oxidative damage to DNA that disrupts normal gene expression in heart
cells. This project studies newly recognized event transcriptional mutagenesis, in which oxidative damaged
DNA produces faulty RNA and proteins that perturb cellular function. Next, this study aims to restore normal
cardiac function by developing targeted DNA repair systems to remove these oxidative DNA lesions and their
widespread detrimental effects leading to HF.

title: Elucidating Mechanisms of Therapy-Resistance to Interferon-alfa in Myeloproliferative Neoplasm Stem Cells
text:
Blood disorders that exhibit overproduction of blood components develop upon the acquisition of genetic
mutations in genes such as CALR and result in disease states called myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN). A
major gap in our understanding of treating patients with MPN is the patient-to-patient variable outcome,
including therapy-resistance to treatments such as interferon-alfa. Here, by applying novel tools that can
sequence many genes in individual cells (`single-cell sequencing') on patient samples and mouse models, we
seek to uncover the mechanisms of therapy-resistance.

title: Blockade of cMYC oncogenic function by pregnancy-induced alterations and remodeling of the mammary gland
text:
Pregnancy has a profound impact on the physiology of a woman's body, in addition to its central role in
reproduction, including a significant effect on the risk of developing breast cancer. In this proposal we will use
mouse models to elucidate novel mechanisms, cell types, and pathways that are altered by pregnancy, and their
involvement in cMYC oncogene function, with the long-term objective of exploiting this knowledge for the future
development of strategies that decrease breast cancer risk in humans.

title: Modulating Endothelial Inflammatory Activation for Atherosclerosis Treatment
text:
This project aims to investigate the critical role of endothelial inflammatory activation in atherosclerosis.
Specifically, we will elucidate how MECOM regulates chromatin remodeling to drive endothelial inflammation,
thereby promoting macrophage adhesion, migration, and polarization. Uncovering these mechanisms will
deepen our understanding of vascular inflammation and establish MECOM as a promising therapeutic target
for atherosclerosis.

title: Identifying Novel Atheroprotective Mechanisms
text:
Public Health Relevance
Atherosclerosis kills more people than any other disease and is caused by cholesterol accumulating in arteries.
Removing excess cholesterol from vascular smooth muscle cells in arteries may prevent atherosclerosis. Our
proposed studies will use strategies that alter cholesterol removal pathways precisely in vascular smooth muscle
cells, which may lead to the development of effective atherosclerosis treatments.
